meta.title: Visited Countries Map From Your Location History
meta.description: See every country you've been to on one map, built from your Google Timeline, GPX or KML files, with days per country. Free and private, in your browser.
meta.keywords: visited countries map, countries visited map, where have I been map, Google Timeline countries, travel map, countries I've been to

intro: Drop in your Google Timeline or GPS files and watch the world fill in: every country you've been to, coloured on the map, with the days you spent in each.

sections.heading: How the map knows where you've been
body: Every point in your file is checked against the borders of 240 countries and territories. Points that fall just off a coastline — a harbour, a beach, a ferry — count for the nearest country, so trips by the sea are not lost.
If your points have timestamps, each country also gets the number of different days you were there, counted in UTC, plus the first and last date.

sections.heading: Get your location history
body: From Google: export Timeline from the Google Maps app on your phone, or use an older Records.json or Semantic Location History file from Google Takeout. Both work here.
From other apps: GPX files from Strava, Garmin, Komoot and most tracking apps, KML or KMZ from Google Earth, FIT and TCX from sports watches, and GeoJSON. You can drop several files at once.

sections.heading: Countries, territories and borders
body: The map includes territories such as Greenland, Puerto Rico or French Polynesia, so the count can be higher than the 195 countries most lists use.

Borders come from Natural Earth at 1:50 million scale. Within about a kilometre of a border a point can land in the neighbouring country, and the smallest states, such as the Vatican, may count as the country around them.

sections.heading: Keep your map growing
body: This tool shows what is in the files you drop in. [Dawarich](/statistics/) does the same with your whole location history and keeps it up to date as you travel: countries and cities per year, a calendar of where you were each day, and the trips behind it.

faqs.a: Yes. It runs in your browser, has no limits and needs no account.
No. Your files are read on your device and never leave it.

faqs.q: Why is a country I visited missing?
faqs.a: The file may not contain points from that trip, for example if location history was off. Very short stops near a border can also land in the neighbouring country.

faqs.q: Why can my count be higher than 195?
faqs.a: Territories such as Greenland or Puerto Rico are counted separately, the way travellers usually count them.
A day counts for every country you have at least one point in on that UTC calendar day, so a day with a border crossing counts for both countries.
